abstract_memory_model.S: P when SS.B=1, or P & 0xFFFF when SS.B=0.
abstract_memory_model.return_ids: r_j = backing(SS, S+j), j=0..3; R={r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3}. Each full four-byte access must be valid; these per-byte descriptions do not silently wrap a crossing operand modulo 2^16.
abstract_memory_model.old_data: X = sum(256^i * M0[d_i], i=0..3). The old four-byte value is read even though the final result is known to be zero.
abstract_memory_model.M1: M1[b] = 0 for b in W; otherwise M1[b] = M0[b]. This is the normal-completion result of the four-byte write, not a claim about byte-store order, atomicity or observations by other agents.
abstract_memory_model.prior_return_word: Q0 = sum(256^j * M0[r_j], j=0..3). Q0 is an arbitrary preexisting return-slot value unless separate caller evidence establishes a pushed offset.
abstract_memory_model.RET_read_after_AND: Q = sum(256^j * M1[r_j], j=0..3) = sum(256^j * (0 if r_j in W else M0[r_j]), j=0..3). The RET read uses the memory resulting from the earlier AND write.
abstract_memory_model.partial_alias: Any nonempty proper subset of return-byte identities may lie in W. Every overlapping return byte becomes zero; nonoverlapping return bytes retain their M0 value under the stated conditions.
abstract_memory_model.full_alias: If every r_j lies in W, Q=0 regardless of Q0.
abstract_memory_model.disjoint_sufficient_condition: W intersect R is empty implies Q=Q0.
abstract_memory_model.exact_preservation_condition: Under this stable ordinary-memory model, Q=Q0 if and only if every overlapping original return byte M0[r_j] with r_j in W was already zero. Disjointness is sufficient but not necessary.
abstract_memory_model.other_caller_memory: The same four-byte write can alias caller locals, saved registers or any other backing memory. No blanket caller-frame preservation follows from the two opcodes.

cases.effect: The four data bytes become zero while the separate return slot retains 0c 67 bf 00.
The AND reads the same initial four bytes as the return word, zeros all four, and RET reads zero. EIP=0 is an explicitly permitted target in this hypothetical model.

unobserved_concrete_models.conclusion: Valid ordinary-memory alias models alter the return offset. The two opcodes alone do not prove return-slot preservation even if a separate caller contract later proves Q0 was pushed by CALL.
